passage: On the fourth-floor bay of the software firm, Shreya walked Himani over to Rishi's desk. "Himani, you know this codebase, and you never make anyone feel silly for asking. Could you pair with Rishi on Tuesdays and Thursdays?" Himani smiled. "Sure. Mornings?" Rishi looked relieved and a little shy. On the first Tuesday, Himani typed while Rishi watched, and then they switched. Himani showed how the team names branches, where the test folder lives, and which reviewer answers fastest. By the third week, Rishi had stopped sending Shreya the same three questions. Shreya's afternoons were quieter, and Rishi's tasks came in on time.

qa.q: On which days do Himani and Rishi pair?
qa.a: They pair on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

qa.q: How did Rishi feel when Himani agreed to pair?
qa.a: Rishi felt relieved and a little shy.

qa.q: What else could Shreya do to help the pairing work, and why?
qa.a: Shreya could check in with both after a month, because the pair may need to change the days or the topics as Rishi grows more confident.

qa.q: How might Himani feel about taking on the buddy role?
qa.a: Himani probably feels trusted and pleased to help, though it takes time out of Himani's own work.

grounding: Illustrates a lead assigning a friendly mid-level colleague to pair with a junior twice a week so the junior learns team habits faster and fewer explanations fall to the lead.

Subject: A favour — pairing with Kunal

Hi Lavanya,

I hope your week is going well. I'd like to ask you something.

As you know, Kunal joined the claims team six weeks ago. He's keen and works hard, but he's still stuck on how we do things here: how we name files, when to update the tracker, who to ask for approvals. I've been explaining the same things to him every day, and it's taking a lot of my time.

You're patient and you know our habits better than anyone. Would you pair with him on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons, for about an hour each, for the next month? Just work alongside him on real cases.

I'll take two of your smaller reports off your plate to make room.

Let me know what you think.

Thanks,
Binita

P.S. Update, four weeks later: Kunal now updates the tracker without reminders, and my inbox is much quieter.

qa.q: Which afternoons did Binita ask Lavanya to pair with Kunal?
Why did Binita decide to ask Lavanya for help?
qa.a: Binita was tired and stretched from explaining the same things every day, and hoped a patient colleague could help Kunal learn faster.

qa.q: What else could Binita do to support Kunal alongside the pairing?
qa.a: Binita could give Kunal small tasks with clear criteria and a short daily check-in, so progress is easy to see.

qa.q: How might Lavanya see Binita's request?
qa.a: Lavanya may feel trusted and valued for being patient, and the offer to take away two reports makes the extra time feel fair.

grounding: It shows a lead asking a friendly mid-level colleague to pair with a junior twice a week, so he learns team habits faster and the lead repeats less.

passage:
Abhinav? Oh, he's doing great now. But you should've seen him in April. I'm Harini, I lead the testing team, and honestly I was the problem at first.
He'd ask me something, I'd explain, and the next day he'd ask again. Where the test data lives, how we log bugs, what a good bug report looks like. I was answering the same things five times a week and getting short with him.
Then I thought, he doesn't need me, he needs someone next to him. So I asked Pranav, who's been with us three years and is the friendliest person on the floor, to sit with Abhinav on Mondays and Wednesdays.
Within a month, Abhinav was writing bug reports that looked like Pranav's. And I got my afternoons back.
Best decision I made that quarter, and I didn't even have to do anything clever.

qa.q: Which days did Pranav sit with Abhinav?
How did Harini feel before arranging the pairing?
qa.a: Harini felt stretched and impatient, getting short with Abhinav after answering the same questions five times a week.

qa.q: What else could Harini have tried first?
qa.a: Harini could have written a short guide to the team's habits, like logging bugs, so Abhinav had something to check before asking.

qa.q: What is the pairing like for Pranav?
qa.a: Pranav takes on extra time with Abhinav, but likely feels trusted as the friendliest person on the floor and sees Abhinav improve quickly.

grounding: It shows a lead assigning a friendly mid-level colleague to pair with a junior twice a week, so he learns team habits faster and the lead saves time.
